What's new in Vekrun 0.7.6

Safer setup
• Setting up a project can no longer give the project's own code administrator rights in the build machine. Before, a dependency's install script could plant a file that a later setup step ran as administrator, and so reach the test secrets you give a project. Now every administrator step starts clean — a fixed set of system folders, nothing from the project or your home folder — services run as an ordinary user with no extra rights, downloads are checked before they are installed, and a Docker Compose service that asks for access to the machine itself is refused with the reason. If the safe setup can't be used, your test secrets are not handed over at all. Every major kind of project (Rails, Node, Django, services, Docker-based tools) was set up again to prove nothing broke.

Share the Map with guests
• While you share a running preview with someone, you can now also let them watch the Factory Map: the plan, the parts being built, verification and progress, live. Turn on "Share the Map with guests" in Live Share. Guests see generic roles (Agent 1, Agent 2, Reviewer, Verifier) — never which AI agents or models you use — and part names stay private unless you choose to show them; even then, file paths and anything that looks like a secret are removed. The Map is shared only while the preview is running and stops the moment it ends. Guests can look, not touch.

Deployment
• A new Deployment page under Plan & Ship. Vekrun finds where your project deploys (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Workers and Pages, Fly.io, Railway, Render, Heroku, DigitalOcean App Platform, Hetzner, AWS App Runner and Amplify, Google Cloud Run), shows whether it's ready (the provider's tool, your token, a valid config), and prepares a plan that says exactly what will go where — before anything happens.
• Nothing is ever deployed without you: each deploy needs your approval in the app, for that exact plan, and is used once. No agent, command line or automation can approve it. Your provider token is kept in your system keychain, can be saved but never read back, and never appears in logs or proof.
• The deploy runs in a fresh, isolated build machine with the provider's official tool, shows each step as it happens, and the result (address, deploy id) is added to the work's proof. If something fails, you see the cause in plain words and one next step.
• Live deploys haven't been tried against real provider accounts yet; the first one you approve is the first real one.

Better context for coding agents
• When Vekrun can't pin down exactly which code a task is about, it now shows the agent short excerpts of the most likely places ("leads to check — not the answer") instead of just names. On our evaluation, the agent received the relevant code in 63 of 102 cases instead of 52, with the same ranking accuracy.
• Context packets repeat themselves less (about 4% smaller), and a packet is never reused after the code it describes has changed — a recovered run now always works from the current code.
